attempted_claim: S_32(SL(2,Z)) has dimension 2 and exactly one Galois orbit of degree 2 (Maeda holds at k=32): the characteristic polynomial of T2 is an irreducible quadratic with non-square discriminant (explicit integer polynomial to be computed and recorded), T3 and T5 characteristic polynomials factored exactly over ZZ, one normalized eigenform q-expansion per orbit to O(q^50) with cubic/quadratic coefficient field made explicit, and sums of computed eigenvalues equal independently computed Eichler-Selberg traces for n=2,3,5.
claim_type: weight-stratum Galois-orbit irreducibility census with Hecke-polynomial and congruence certificates
decisive_failure: originality: The mathematical facts claimed are already published/tabled. Ghitza-McAndrew (arXiv:1207.3480, retrieved live) verifies T2-irreducibility for all level-one weights <12000 including k=32 via Sage, directly implying the draft's central 'single Galois orbit degree 2 / Maeda holds at k=32' and T2 quadratic irreducibility. The draft itself concedes 'This is not a new proof of Maeda's conjecture in general; T2-irreducibility to weight <12000 is due to Ghitza-McAndrew, and the same polynomials appear in LMFDB (1.32.a.a)'. Thus chi_T2=T^2-39960T-2235350016, chi_T3, chi_T5, field Q(sqrt(18295489)) with discriminant 18295489=67*273067, and O(q^50) eigenforms are LMFDB-tabled data, not new orbit counts, degrees, fields, or polynomials. Tsaknias (arXiv:1205.3420) and Martin (arXiv:1912.06911) show Maeda-type orbit-counting is established prior art (higher-level speculation and on-average level-aspect conjecture respectively), while Citro-Ghitza (DOI 10.1112/s1461157013000132, retrieved live via Crossref) shows systematic level-one Hecke eigensystem enumeration already existed (mod-p). The only delta is packaging: one stdlib-only script bundling T2/T3/T5 polys + O(q^50) + trace cross-check + mod-29 witness 'checkable without Sage/Magma/PARI'. Repackaging known weight-32 values in a different language with an extra trace-formula consistency check does not create a new Galois orbit, new polynomial, or new irreducibility theorem; fixing k=32 inside an already-verified <12000 range is parameter selection, not a new result. Hence originality FAIL. value: Even taken as correct, the result is not independently worth finding later. It is a textbook exercise plus table lookup: dim via floor(k/12) and C[E4,E6] monomials, Hecke action via standard q-expansion formula, discriminant non-square plus mod-p check, and quoted Eichler-Selberg formula validated at only 4 points (n=1,2,3,5) with general-n correctness assumed. No L-function, Galois-representation, or congruence consequence is proved (limitations concede this). The weight k=32 is an unmotivated single parameter inside the already-settled <12000 verification; the method is claimed reusable for 24<=k<=36 but not demonstrated. L-function workers already have a trusted, more extensive anchor in LMFDB 1.32.a.a (q-expansions, Hecke data, field x^2-x-4573872 with discriminant 18295489); a seconds-scale stdlib replay of the same numbers adds engineering convenience, not scientific insight, and the draft's own rejection-risks anticipate 'textbook restatement / duplicate of LMFDB / mere parameter choice k=32 / brute-force table without insight'. Under SCOPE value gates this is textbook restatement + mere parameter substitution + unexplained/already-tabled enumeration with tiny unmotivated gain, even if correct and even if the bundle were deemed new. Hence value FAIL.

problem_statement: Fix the level-one weight stratum k=32 (dim S_32(SL(2,Z))=2; note brief's 'dim 3' applies to k=36, corrected here via dim formula). Determine the exact Galois-orbit decomposition of the cuspidal Hecke eigenforms: orbit count and degrees, exact factored characteristic polynomials over ZZ of T2,T3,T5, one normalized (a1=1) q-expansion to O(q^50) per orbit with coefficient-field discriminant, Maeda-type irreducibility decision for this k (T2 quadratic irreducible vs split), and independent Eichler-Selberg trace-formula cross-check of Tr(Tn) for n=2,3,5 against modular-symbols linear algebra over Q, all produced by a single Sage script rerunnable in minutes.
